body.statement: Can the perspective tangent-program handle weaken uniform Slater regularity to a sharp facial metric-regularity condition while retaining uniform Hadamard directional differentiability of \(P\mapsto(C_P(t))_{t\in\mathcal T_0}\) through zero primal cells, nonunique optimizers, and moving odds faces, and can a uniformly consistent \(\widehat{\mathfrak T}_n\) yield derivative-bootstrap bands that attain the \(n^{-1/2}\) regular-profile diameter? Near the finite-to-infinite boundary, can one construct an adaptive exact multinomial or Poisson--Gaussian hybrid inversion whose extended-real behavior matches the two-point lower bound?
body.justification: This is the open efficiency and adaptation step beyond the proved regular finite-sample diameter and the boundary impossibility result.
body.gap: DuanZhangZhang2018SOCP assumes finite value, compact optimizers, and Slater regularity; FangSantos2019Directional and FirpoGalvaoParker2023Value require a stable finite-valued application-specific derivative. None treats this facially degenerate extended-real perspective frontier.
body.consumer: The result would provide simultaneous uncertainty quantification fine enough to compare scientifically relevant budgets across the full categorical sensitivity curve.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniform Hadamard directional differentiability and uniform consistency of the estimated frontier derivative through zero perspective cells, nonunique optimizers, and moving odds faces, together with an adaptive exact inversion at the extended-real boundary.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen regularity assumptions supply a uniform Slater margin only on the named regular region. Outside it, they give neither a facial metric-regularity modulus nor an active-set separation condition, so optimizer correspondences and tangent cones can change discontinuously; the boundary pair also proves that no uniformly honest finite-width continuation can cover the finite-to-infinite transition.
obligation.attempted: Linearized the margin and ATE equations on fixed optimizer faces, retained the closed perspective recession term on zero cells, and enlarged active odds sets. This closes pointwise fixed-face programs but gives no uniform face-identification or metric-regularity bound over the class in the open question.
obligation.partial_result: The frozen assumptions prove two complementary results. On \(\Theta_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)\), the whole frontier profile has a simultaneous finite-sample band of width at most \(2L_{\mathrm{reg}}(\delta)r_n=O(n^{-1/2})\). At the specified finite-to-infinite null boundary, every confidence set honest at the contiguous pair has infinite diameter with limiting probability at least \(1-2\alpha\). These premises do not determine a uniformly estimable tangent operator on the intervening facially degenerate class.
